name: Starter: Korean
about: Korean word order in real, everyday sentences: the verb last, and the particles that say who does what.

words.우리: we; our (often my, for family and home)
words.없다: to not be there, to not have
words.수: possibility or ability (bound noun in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다, 'can/cannot')
words.많다: to be many, to be a lot

mannaseo-bangawoyo.about: What you say when you meet someone: literally, meeting you, I'm glad.

jal-meokgesseumnida.en: Thank you for the food (before eating).
jal-meokgesseumnida.about: Said before a meal, to whoever made or paid for it: literally, I will eat well. After the meal: 잘 먹었습니다.

items.means: One tea and one water, please.

items.text: 물을 마시고 싶어요. 물 좀 주세요.

물를 마시고 싶어요. 물 좀 주세요.

concept.line: 은 (after a consonant) or 는 (after a vowel) marks what the sentence is about, or a contrast; it isn't the same as an English subject, and Korean often leaves I and you unsaid.

words.means: a little; some; softens a request ('please')

concept.line: A yes/no question usually keeps the statement's order and polite ending, and the voice often rises; a question word stays where its answer would.

words.means: 선생님이에요 = am a teacher; 선생님이세요 = are a teacher; 선생님이 = a teacher
학생이에요 = am a student; 학생이 = a student
엄마예요 = is my mom; 엄마는 = my mom
아빠예요 = is my dad; 아빠는 = my dad

concept.line: A noun with 이에요 (after a consonant) or 예요 (after a vowel) says what something is.

words.means: 여동생이 = a younger sister; 여동생은 = younger sister

concept.line: The verb ends the sentence; who, what, where and when all come before it.
을 or 를 marks what the verb acts on, and it comes before the verb.

words.means: 집에 = in a house; 집은 = house

concept.line: 에 after a place means to it, or where something is; after a time it means when.

words.means: possibility or ability (bound noun in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다, 'can/cannot')
가야 = must go; 갈 = to go
